intelligence.enrichment: Filtration separates solid particles from a liquid by passing the mixture through a strainer, cloth, filter paper, or other filter with pores that hold back the particles and let the liquid pass. Pores in the filter allow smaller liquid portions through while retaining solid particles that are too large for the pores. The learner correctly applies this rule: Filtration separates solid particles from a liquid by passing the mixture through a strainer, cloth, filter paper, or other filter with pores that hold back the particles and let the liquid pass. All filters work the same way, so any strainer or cloth should make muddy water clear.
